claim: Electrically coupled neural networks like in mammalian inferior olive nucleus generate synchronized rhythmic activity by the subthreshold sinusoidal-like oscillations of the membrane voltage.
source: Recent experimental studies showed that electrically coupled neural networks like in mammalian inferior olive nucleus generate synchronized rhythmic activity by the subthreshold sinusoidal-like oscillations of the membrane voltage.
evidence: The claim is attributed to recent experimental studies, indicating citation-based support.

claim: The structural anatomical connectome of Caenorhabditis elegans was completely known recently.
source: Inspired by these necessities of developing a theoretical and computational model to this end and, however, in the absence of connectome information for the inferior olive nucleus, here we investigated interference phenomena of the subthreshold oscillations in the reference system Caenorhabditis elegans for which the structural anatomical connectome was completely known recently.
evidence: The claim references the recent completion of C. elegans connectome information, supported by citation to Cook et al., 2019 elsewhere in the manuscript.

claim: The transmission of all cell-pairs disappeared beyond a threshold wavenumber.
source: Also, we unraveled that (1) the transmission of all cell-pairs disappeared beyond a threshold wavenumber
evidence: This is a primary finding from the computational model presented in the study.

claim: Long distance and regular patterned transmission existed in the body-wall muscles part of the model network.
source: (2) long distance and regular patterned transmission existed in the body-wall muscles part of the model network
evidence: This is a primary finding from the computational model analysis.

claim: Major hub cell-pairs of the transmission were identified for many wavenumber conditions.
source: (3) major hub cell-pairs of the transmission were identified for many wavenumber conditions.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the computational model analysis.

claim: Electrical synapses change the membrane potential of neurons through ion current flowing through the gap junction between neurons.
source: The ion current flowing through the gap junction between neurons changes the membrane potential of those neurons, which is called signal transmission by electrical synapses (Carew and Kandel, 1976).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Carew and Kandel, 1976.

claim: Electrical synapses have characteristics such as simple structure, fast signal transmission, bidirectional communication (in most cases), and a wide operation range for voltage including the subthreshold region.
source: Electrical synapses have characteristics such as simple structure, fast signal transmission, bidirectional communication (in most cases), and a wide operation range for voltage including the subthreshold region (Bennett, 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bennett, 1997.

claim: Electrical synapses play various roles, such as excitation or inhibition of neurons, synchronization or desynchronization of neural activity, promotion or attenuation of rhythms, and improvement of signal-to-noise ratio.
source: Based on this, it has been reported that electrical synapses play various roles, such as excitation or inhibition of neurons, synchronization or desynchronization of neural activity, promotion or attenuation of rhythms, and improvement of signal-to-noise ratio (Connors, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Connors, 2017.

claim: Spontaneous and robust subthreshold membrane potential oscillations were observed in the inferior olivary cells.
source: Spontaneous and robust subthreshold membrane potential oscillations were observed in the inferior olivary cells (Benardo and Foster, 1986; Chorev et al., 2007; Devor and Yarom, 2002; Lampl and Yarom, 1997; Llinás and Yarom, 1981).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: The inferior olivary cells are intra-connected only by electrical synapses.
source: The inferior olivary cells are intra-connected only by electrical synapses, and it was reported that the presence of electrical synapses is largely involved in the synchronization of subthreshold oscillations (De Zeeuw et al., 2003; Leznik and Llinás, 2005; Leznik et al., 2002; Llinás, 2013; Long et al., 2002; Turecek et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The presence of electrical synapses is largely involved in the synchronization of subthreshold oscillations in inferior olivary cells.
source: The inferior olivary cells are intra-connected only by electrical synapses, and it was reported that the presence of electrical synapses is largely involved in the synchronization of subthreshold oscillations (De Zeeuw et al., 2003; Leznik and Llinás, 2005; Leznik et al., 2002; Llinás, 2013; Long et al., 2002; Turecek et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Information on the indexing of all individual neurons, muscles, and organ cells present in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans and the entire connectivity between those cells by chemical and electrical synapses was recently updated.
source: In the field of connectome, information on the indexing of all individual neurons, muscles, and organ cells present in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans and the entire connectivity between those cells by chemical and electrical synapses was recently updated (Cook et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cook et al., 2019.

claim: The C. elegans connectome data identifies connectivity weights proportional to the structural size of each synapse, with 1433 electrical synapses present among a total of 469 cells.
source: This available connectome data of C. elegans identifies connectivity weights proportional to the structural size of each synapse, with 1433 electrical synapses present among a total of 469 cells, including neurons, muscles, pharynx, and other organ cells.
evidence: The claim is based on the connectome data from Cook et al., 2019.

claim: During the gentle nose touch response in C. elegans, nose mechanoreceptor neurons connected to electrical synapses simultaneously increased in activity, thereby serving as a coincidence detector.
source: During the gentle nose touch response, nose mechanoreceptor neurons connected to electrical synapses simultaneously increased in activity, thereby serving as a coincidence detector (Chatzigeorgiou and Schafer, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chatzigeorgiou and Schafer, 2011.

claim: A pair of GABAergic motor neurons controlling the bowel movement program repeated every 50 s in C. elegans used synchronized activity through electrical synapses at their axon terminal.
source: And a pair of GABAergic motor neurons controlling the bowel movement program repeated every 50 s used synchronized activity through electrical synapses at their axon terminal (Choi et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Choi et al., 2021.

claim: Direct observation or indirect evidence of spontaneous subthreshold oscillations has NOT been confirmed in C. elegans.
source: However, direct observation or indirect evidence of spontaneous subthreshold oscillations has NOT been confirmed in C. elegans.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of evidence in the literature.

claim: Subthreshold oscillations have wave properties as fluctuations observed in membrane potential measurements and experience interference when propagated in the neural tissue space.
source: Likewise, it is experimentally confirmed that subthreshold oscillations have wave properties as fluctuations observed in membrane potential measurements and experience interference when propagated in the neural tissue space (Chiang and Durand, 2023; Gupta et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The Anderson localization phenomenon is a general wave phenomenon due to the wave interference between multiple scattering paths.
source: In the field of physics, the Anderson localization phenomenon has been well known, and it is a general wave phenomenon due to the wave interference between multiple scattering paths.
evidence: This is established knowledge in physics.

claim: Depending on the strength of the scattering of waves, the result of wave interference could be constructive or destructive, namely, waves could transmit or localize through the media, correspondingly.
source: Depending on the strength of the scattering of waves, the result of wave interference could be constructive or destructive, namely, waves could transmit or localize through the media, correspondingly.
evidence: This is established knowledge about wave interference.

claim: The theoretical and numerical method for describing the Anderson localization problem usually employed the tight-binding Anderson Hamiltonian.
source: The theoretical and numerical method for describing the so-called Anderson localization problem usually employed the tight-binding Anderson Hamiltonian.
evidence: This is established knowledge in physics, supported by citations.

claim: Most of the strong transmissions were found in the cell-pairs of intra-body-wall muscles at E=0.225.
source: Here, we confirmed that not all cell-pairs transmit the wave signals with even transmission coefficients. Most of the strong transmissions were found in the cell-pairs of intra-body-wall muscles, and a small number of cells belonging to sensory neurons, motor neurons, and other organ cells also showed strong transmission in cell-pairs between them or to body-wall muscles.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study, referring to Figure 2B.

claim: All cells were isolated separately without exchanging the wave signals with each other at E=5.650.
source: As expected, all cells were isolated separately without exchanging the wave signals with each other, and the entire circuit stop transmitting wave signals of this wavenumber.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study, referring to Figure 2C.

claim: The region of the cell-pairs with strong transmission changed depending on the value of E (or wavenumber), which was named 'Wavenumber-Dependent Transmission Map (WDTM) of subthreshold waves on the electrical synapse network model'.
source: As expected above, the region of the cell-pairs with strong transmission changed depending on the value of E (or wavenumber), which we named 'Wavenumber-Dependent Transmission Map (WDTM) of subthreshold waves on the electrical synapse network model'.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: In the E value range of [1.275, 1.575], only the cell-pairs of intra-strand were found in the WDTMs.
source: Following this classification, the cell-pairs of both intra- and inter-strand were found in the WDTMs of the E value range of [0, 0.350] (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2A, B), whereas only the cell-pairs of intra-strand were found in the WDTMs in the E value range of [1.275, 1.575] (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: Cell-pairs with regular patterned transmission of the body-wall muscles were observed in the WDTMs of the E value range of [1.275, 1.575].
source: In the WDTMs of the E value range of [1.275, 1.575], cell-pairs with regular patterned transmission of the body-wall muscles were observed through the network diagram (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: The head mesodermal cell (hmc) seemed to play an important role in building a bridge between inter-strand cell-pairs of the body-wall muscles.
source: On the other hand, when the cell-pairs of inter-strand of the body-wall muscles appeared in the WDTMs as shown in Figure 3A, B, the head mesodermal cell (hmc) seemed to play an important role in building a bridge between them.
evidence: This is an inference from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: hmc was strongly connected near the neck of the body-wall muscles (seventh and eighth muscles) for all four strands.
source: This would be recognized from the network diagram itself of black edges without WDTM, and hmc was strongly connected near the neck of the body-wall muscles (seventh and eighth muscles) for all four strands.
evidence: This is a finding from the network diagram analysis.

claim: Most of the cell-pairs in Appendix 1—table 5 showed the kinds of short distances 1–3, which consisted of various cell types.
source: Most of the cell-pairs in Appendix 1—table 5 showed the kinds of short distances 1–3, which consisted of various cell types.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: The cell-pairs with long distances in Appendix 1—table 5 ranging from 4 to 17 were mainly pairs between hmc and body-wall muscles.
source: On the other hand, the cell-pairs with long distances in Appendix 1—table 5 ranging from 4 to 17 were mainly pairs between hmc and body-wall muscles.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: The strong transmission between hmc and the tail muscle, which corresponds to the longest distance, passes through the intra-strand connections from the neck to the tail of body-wall muscles.
source: The strong transmission between hmc and the tail muscle, which corresponds to the longest distance, passes through the intra-strand connections from the neck to the tail of body-wall muscles.
evidence: This is an inference from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: One inter neuron (AVBR) and two motor neurons (AS11 and VD04) formed a cell-pair with the body-wall muscles with strong transmission and long distance.
source: In there, one inter neuron (AVBR) and two motor neurons (AS11 and VD04) formed a cell-pair with the body-wall muscles, respectively, and four sensory neurons (CEPDL, IL1R, IL1DR, and OLQDL) formed cell-pairs between them.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: Four sensory neurons (CEPDL, IL1R, IL1DR, and OLQDL) formed cell-pairs between them with strong transmission and long distance.
source: In there, one inter neuron (AVBR) and two motor neurons (AS11 and VD04) formed a cell-pair with the body-wall muscles, respectively, and four sensory neurons (CEPDL, IL1R, IL1DR, and OLQDL) formed cell-pairs between them.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: A cell-pair was declared as a major hub cell-pair if the average appearance rate of a cell-pair was 0.1 or higher.
source: In this study, we declared a cell-pair as a major hub cell-pair if the average appearance rate of a cell-pair was 𝑥 < 0 or higher.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study. Note: There appears to be a typo in the manuscript ('𝑥 < 0' should likely be '0.1').

claim: The major hub cell-pairs were the cell-pairs of intra-strand of the body-wall muscles.
source: The major hub cell-pairs were the cell-pairs of intra-strand of the body-wall muscles (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: The edges of each strand of the body-wall muscles from the neck (seventh or eighth muscle) to the tail (twenty-third or twenty-fourth muscle) were simply connected in a line.
source: As seen in the network diagram, the edges of each strand of the body-wall muscles from the neck (seventh or eighth muscle) to the tail (twenty-third or twenty-fourth muscle) were simply connected in a line, unlike the messy edges among most neurons in the network (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the network diagram analysis.

claim: The complexity of connections among most neurons increase with the number of transmissible paths of wave propagation, and the sum of phase changes coming from various path-length differences causes the deconstructive interference.
source: In general, the complexity of connections among most neurons increase with the number of transmissible paths of wave propagation, and the sum of phase changes coming from various path-length differences causes the deconstructive interference.
evidence: This is a general principle applied to interpret the findings.

claim: The simple (or regular) connections in each strand of the body-wall muscles from the neck to the tail reduced the number of transmissible paths of wave signals, which suppressed deconstructive interference and thus resulted in the strong transmission for various wavenumbers.
source: Therefore, the simple (or regular) connections in each strand of the body-wall muscles from the neck to the tail reduced the number of transmissible paths of wave signals, which suppressed deconstructive interference and thus resulted in the strong transmission for various wavenumbers.
evidence: This is an inference from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: The cell-pairs between hmc and the neck of the ventral-left strand of the body-wall muscles were identified as major hub cell-pair.
source: Also, the cell-pairs between hmc and the neck of the ventral-left strand of the body-wall muscles were also identified as major hub cell-pair (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: The edges between hmc and the neck muscles were very strong compared to other edges.
source: As seen in the network diagram, since the edges between hmc and the neck muscles were very strong compared to other edges (Figure 3), the relative contribution of wave signals coming from other cells could be almost ignored, and thus resulted in the strong transmission for various wavenumbers.
evidence: This is a finding from the network diagram analysis.

claim: The cell-pairs among two sensory neurons (PVDL and PVDR) and three other organ cells (CANL, CANR, exc_cell) were identified as major hub cell-pairs.
source: The cell-pairs among two sensory neurons (PVDL and PVDR) and three other organ cells (CANL, CANR, exc_cell) were also identified as major hub cell-pairs (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: The strong edge shown on the network diagram was not a sufficient condition to implicate a major hub cell-pair.
source: Therefore, the strong edge shown on the network diagram was not a sufficient condition to implicate a major hub cell-pair.
evidence: This is an inference from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: Several inter neurons and other organ cells showed high effective conductance, while pharynx, body-wall muscles from the neck to the tail, and sex-specific muscles showed very low effective conductance.
source: Several inter neurons and other organ cells showed high effective conductance, while pharynx, body-wall muscles from the neck to the tail, and sex-specific muscles showed very low effective conductance (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from the effective conductance analysis presented in the study.

claim: Inter neurons have many complex connections among them, which act as parallel connections of multiple electrical resistors, resulting in lower effective resistance (or higher effective conductance).
source: Since inter neurons have many complex connections among them, many electrical current paths exist between the two inter neurons, which act as parallel connections of multiple electrical resistors. This results in lower effective resistance (or higher effective conductance).
evidence: This is an inference from the effective conductance analysis.

claim: For a situation with considering the interference, many transmissible forward and backward paths of the signal propagation rather caused the deconstructive interference, preventing the transmission of the signal.
source: However, for a situation with considering the interference, many transmissible forward and backward paths of the signal propagation rather caused the deconstructive interference, preventing the transmission of the signal.
evidence: This is an inference from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: Wave signals were effectively delivered only within a small number of very strongly connected cell groups (PVDL/R, CANL/R, exc_cell, and hmc) or within a large number of very regularly connected cell groups (body-wall muscle strands from the neck to the tail).
source: Wave signals were effectively delivered only within a small number of very strongly connected cell groups (PVDL/R, CANL/R, exc_cell, and hmc) or within a large number of very regularly connected cell groups (body-wall muscle strands from the neck to the tail).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis presented in the study.

claim: No synchronized rhythmic activity induced by subthreshold membrane potential oscillations has been reported for C. elegans so far.
source: In this study, we used the structural anatomical information from C. elegans' electrical synapse network, but no synchronized rhythmic activity induced by subthreshold membrane potential oscillations has been reported for C. elegans so far.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of evidence in the literature.

claim: There might be an electrical synapse network in the mammalian inferior olive nucleus that connect cells very strongly or very regularly.
source: As to the synchronized rhythmic activation observed like in the mammalian inferior olive nucleus, we think that there might be an electrical synapse network in there that connect cells very strongly or very regularly.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the study's findings.

claim: The constructive interference of subthreshold membrane potential waves with a specific wavenumber may generate the synchronized rhythmic activation.
source: The plausible possibility according to our model study is that the constructive interference of subthreshold membrane potential waves with a specific wavenumber may generate the synchronized rhythmic activation.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the study's findings.

claim: The weights were proportional to the spatial size of the corresponding gap junction.
source: The weights were proportional to the spatial size of the corresponding gap junction, which we hypothesized that the larger the weight, the stronger the connection between the cells and thus the better transmit the wave signal to the connected cell.
evidence: This is based on the connectome data and a hypothesis made by the authors.

claim: Two virtual nodes (VNs) were inserted between each pair of cells connected by a gap junction in the circuit model.
source: Each gap junction connected to a cell-pair was treated as an edge connecting two nodes in our circuit, and we inserted two virtual nodes (VNs) between those two nodes to be connected sequentially through VNs (Cell-VN-VN-Cell).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in constructing the circuit model.

claim: All edges inside the circuit were set to have the identical length a.
source: Here, all edges inside our circuit were set to have the identical length a.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in constructing the circuit model.

claim: In the circuit model, the weight of the edge meant the transmission coefficient of the signal transmitted through this edge.
source: In our circuit model, the weight of the edge meant the transmission coefficient of the signal transmitted through this edge, so if the weight was 1 corresponded to complete transmission, and 0 corresponded to complete reflection (or unavailable edge), respectively.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in constructing the circuit model.

claim: Within the circuit, the characteristic of the signal being spontaneously attenuated, and disappearing was excluded.
source: And within our circuit, the characteristic of the signal being spontaneously attenuated, and disappearing was excluded.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in constructing the circuit model.

claim: When a signal incoming from the outside to a node in the circuit was reflected to the outside at the same node and simultaneously transmitted to the outside at another node, the sum of the transmission and reflection coefficients to the outside always remained at 1 without loss.
source: Therefore, when a signal incoming from the outside to a node in our circuit was reflected to the outside at the same node and simultaneously transmitted to the outside at another node, the sum of the transmission and reflection coefficients to the outside always remained at 1 without loss.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in constructing the circuit model.

claim: The newly constructed tight-binding Anderson Hamiltonian for the circuit was represented as a matrix of 3335 by 3335.
source: Since the total number of the cells was 469, and we inserted two VNs for every 1433 electrical synapses, the newly constructed tight-binding Anderson Hamiltonian for our circuit was represented as a matrix of 3335 by 3335.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the computational model.

claim: The errors in the calculation correspond to 0.006% of the total calculation results.
source: We performed the calculations on a total of 109,746 cell-pairs for a total of 801 E values, so these errors correspond to 0.006% of the total calculation results.
evidence: This describes errors in the computational analysis.
